items.text: Thanks to its high print resolution and dimensional stability, PLA MINERAL is an excellent choice for architectural, artistic, and model-making studios, as well as for all applications requiring faithful detail reproduction—from scale models and sculptures to precision prototypes. The material allows for aesthetic finishes: prints can be further processed, such as sanding or staining, which provides great freedom in creating a final effect reminiscent of a traditional plaster cast.
items.conditions: Maker statement only; no application validation, exposure test or suitability established. Specific conditions not published.

items.text: Its plaster-like finish makes models look like traditional castings—with a natural, matte texture and clear reproduction of even the finest details.

Of the solvents studied, chloroform is the best solvent for quickly preparing 10 % wt/vol solutions of all Ingeo grades and morphologies; 4032D pellets and injection-moulded bars were readily transformed to 10 % wt/vol solutions in chloroform in 2-4 hours at room temperature
items.conditions: 10 % wt/vol mixture, shaken at 175 rpm at room temperature; some samples stirred at 65 °C
items.note: Study grades: 4060D (12 % D, amorphous), 2003D (4.5 % D) and 4032D (1.6 % D, crystallisable) as pellets and injection-moulded bars; no filament grade was tested. A printed part is largely amorphous, so the amorphous-bar results are the nearer case. The reference reports dissolution; the verdict word "soluble" is reserved for water, so dissolution in an organic solvent is recorded as not-resistant.

items.text: Ingeo biopolymers will burn. Clear to white smoke is produced when product burns. Toxic fumes are released under conditions of incomplete combustion.
items.note: No UL 94 rating is stated. Verdict convention used in this table: burns / UL 94 HB = not-resistant, V-1 or V-2 = limited, V-0 = resistant.

items.text: In-line drying is required. A moisture content of less than 0.025 % (250 ppm) is recommended to prevent viscosity degradation. Typical drying conditions are 4 hours at 80 °C (175 °F) to a dew point of -40 °C (-40 °F).
items.note: A processing threshold (hydrolytic loss of melt viscosity), not an equilibrium water uptake; the percentage in the finding is the recommended maximum before melting.
